narr: Monsoon moisture over northern Arizona and Utah brought showers and thunderstorms to those areas. This caused several spikes to the Paria River at the confluence of the Colorado River. There also were several spikes in the flow in the days before this episode.
ev: Heavy rain over far northern Arizona and south-central Utah caused several spikes on the Paria River just before it joined the Colorado River upstream from The Grand Canyon. The water flow started to increase (from 4.98 feet) around 100 PM MST on August 13. There were three crests in the flow: 6.24 feet at 500 PM, 704 feet at 800 PM MST on August 13, and 7.66 feet at 300 AM MST on August 14. The flow returned to near normal at around 1100 PM on August 14.
lsr: The Paria River at Lees Ferry rose 1.5 feet according to a USGS stream gauge due to upstream heavy rainfall.
